story_pergunta: At your company, who reviews the code the AI writes?

slides.eyebrow: AI ON THE RISE · VIBE CODING SECURITY
slides.headline: A demo in a day. A data breach in production.
slides.sub: Researchers found passports and 200K chats exposed in Lovable apps.

slides.headline: Researchers checked 159,041 Lovable projects
slides.body: Crissy Field GmbH found sensitive data readable without a login. Examples: 80,000+ forum profiles, 200,000+ chat messages, and 1,000+ records with passport numbers. They could not establish whether any of it was misused.

slides.label: sites with email records exposed, out of 24,664 examined closely
slides.sub: That is 30%, but the researchers say it is not a confirmed leak rate.

slides.headline: What I see in companies shipping AI-built apps
items: The app works in the demo, so nobody asks who can read the data behind it
Access rules are nobody's job once the prototype goes live
Nobody reviews the code the AI wrote before real customers use it

slides.headline: How the AskMoses.AI development team ships AI-written code
items: Every dev works with Claude Code on the project
Another Claude reviews every pull request; the human decides on business grounds
Deploys on Vercel with 1-click rollback and daily backups

slides.headline: Simple that works beats complex that impresses.
slides.body: Speed is not the risk. Shipping without a review step is. The researchers say access permissions must be reviewed before an app handles real data. In practice, that means review and a safe way to roll back are part of the process from day one.

slides.eyebrow: WANT TO SEE HOW I DID IT?
slides.headline: Comment CLAUDE.
slides.body: I'll send you the step-by-step of this case by DM. I take AI off the drawing board and put it into production, with measured results.

caption:
A research team analyzed 159,041 Lovable projects and found sensitive data readable without a login. Examples: a forum exposing 80,000+ profiles and 200,000+ chat messages, and a service provider exposing 1,000+ records with passport details. The researchers could not establish whether any of it was misused, and they say the 30% figure is not a confirmed leak rate.

My reading: vibe coding gets you to a demo in a day. Production needs access rules, security review and measurement. Without them, speed turns into a data breach.

This is a problem I had to solve. The AskMoses.AI development team is 100% agentic. Every dev works with Claude Code on the project. Another Claude reviews the pull request. The human decides on business grounds, not technical ones. Deploys run on Vercel with 1-click rollback and daily backups.

The question is not whether AI writes your code. It is who checks it before customers rely on it.

Comment CLAUDE and I'll DM you how I did it.

Sources: crissyfield.de
